records.resourcesInterview:
1. Carefully study the types of questions that converted candidates on this PGDBA WordPress page similar to your own profile have been asked previously in PIs.
2. Your motivation for joining this course will be studied very closely by the 3 panelists. Have a very clear opinion on why you want to join this course in particular.
3. Revise Higher Maths topics, specifically Linear Algebra, Basic Statistics and Probability.
4. For Freshers - you may be asked more questions on your grad - level subjects, your internship, any project you did, so be better prepared in that domain. For Experienced folks -  you may be asked more questions related to your workex, and regarding the domain you're from, so you may plan your preparation accordingly.
5. Finally - no amount of preparation will guarantee that you have an answer to everything asked by the panelists. If you don't know the answer, don't fret and tell them so rather than beating around the bush.

Q1. What do your parents call you? In how many ways can this name be permuted? Explain this formula intuitively.
A: 5! / 2!
Q2. What are the types of errors in Hypothesis Testing?
A: Type 1 and Type 2 error.
Q3. (Gave a problem) What is the type 1 error of this problem?
A: Was unable to solve, so told the panelist that i was unable to arrive at an answer, and explained my approach to him.
Q4. Let's say you want to estimate the number of Red colored Maruti Altos running in your city. How will you approach this problem?
A:
* The population of my city is approx. 1.8 Cr.
* Let's say there are 5 members per family. Therefore total families = 1.8Cr / 5 = 36L.
* Let's say that there is 1 car per 2 families. Therefore total cars = 36L / 2 = 18L.
* Maruti Suzuki has a market share of about 50% in Delhi. Therefore total Maruti cars in Delhi = 18L * 50% = 9L
* Alto has been one of the best selling cars of Maruti Suzuki. Let's say 10% of all maruti sales have been that of Alto. Therefore total Alto cars in Delhi = 9L * 10% = 90,000
* Since Red is not a common color, let's say only 2% of the Alto cars sold in delhi were of Red color. Therefore total red colored Maruti Alto in my city ~ 1800 cars.

Go through previous year interview experiences and prepare accordingly. Prepare well for profile-based questions and be clear on why you want to do PGDBA. In Maths, prepare 2-3 topics really well (particularly probability, linear algebra) so that you can tell the panel if you are asked to choose topics.
It is okay if you are unable to answer a question. But for the questions which you know, yours answer should be very clear.

questions.general:
Q: Introduce yourself
A: Well prepared answer
Q: Why do you want to leave AstraZeneca and do PGDBA?
A: Told how I developed interest in analytics and that I have been following applications of analytics.
Q: So you are not interested in doing a management course.
A: Explained how I can contribute to an organization using the knowledge gained through this course.
Q:Give some examples of the applications which you read recently.
A: Explained about the applications of analytics in pharma/healthcare sector.
Q:Your interest seem to be more on healthcare.
A: Gave some examples of analytics in finance.
Q: Why do you think there is more focus on analytics in recent days when these methods were existing from long?
A: Huge amount of data generated everyday now and better processing speed.
Q: How were decisions made earlier without these techniques?
A: Based on intuition and human experience/knowledge and not based on data.
questions.mathStats:
Q: Which topics are you comfortable with in Maths?
A: Permutations & Combinations, Probability & Random variables
Q: What is a Random variable? Give some examples.
A: Answered with example.
Q: What is a probability distribution? What are the types of distribution that you know?
A: Answered.
Q: What is Binomial distribution?
A: Explained with examples of coin tossing and probability of getting r heads out of n tosses.
Q: If you toss the coin repeatedly and want to find the probability of getting first heads, how will you calculate that?
A: Answered using Geometric distribution.
Q: Do you know about memorylessness property?
A:  Have read about it, but couldn't recollect.
Q: Do you know about calculus?
A: Yes, 11th 12th level Differential and Integral calculus.
Q: Do you know about matrices?
A: Yes
Q: What is rank of a matrix? What is the significance of it?
A: Rank - Number of linearly independent rows or columns in a matrix.  Denotes the information content in a matrix
Q: For a 3 x 2 matrix, what is the maximum rank that it can take?
A: 2, Maximum rank = min(m,n) for a m x n matrix
Q: How will you calculate rank of a matrix?
A: Explained rank calculation using row-echelon form
Q: Do you know how to solve system of linear equations using matrices?
A: Yes. Explained
Q: If you have a 3x4 matrix can you find the determinant? Can you solve the linear equations of a 3x4 matrix?
A: No. It’s not possible to get a unique solution for a set of 3 equations with 4 variables

questions.mathStats:
1. Can you prove the empirical formula of measures of central tendencies?
Ans. The formula is Mode = 3*Median - 2*Mean. It is only an observational result that Karl Pearson concluded after performing a large number of tests on different data. Hence, it has no mathematical proof.
2. What is the difference between local minima and global minima?
I could not give a clear answer to that as they were not satisfied with the basic understanding I had about it.
3. What are the difference and the similarity between Standard Normal Distribution and Normal Distribution?
Ans. Normal Distribution can have any mean and variance but Standard Normal Distribution has a mean of 0 and variance 1. The Mean, Median and Mode are all same for both distributions.
(The entire panel disagreed with my answer but I did not change my answer because I knew it was right)

questions.mathStats:
1a. I mentioned that I was interested in sports, and the mathematics behind it in my introduction. The interviewer asked me to give my opinion on whether the batting average in cricket is a good measure of the batsman's 'average' run-scoring performance, as it does not take into account the number of innings when the batsman remained not out.
- Explained that the term given for the measure can be a bit misleading if considered as an average per inning, as per my understanding, it actually is a measure of how many runs a batsman scores before getting dismissed (between two successive dismissals)
1b. The interviewer asked me to then suggest a better metric for measuring the per inning average score by the batsman.
- Suggested the use of quartile scores.
1c. Can we give make a rewarding adjustment to the batsman's score if he remains not out, comparing it with his current average performance?
- Each inning is affected by a multitude of factors, rewarding on the basis of just the historical performance may not be the most optimal choice. If a reward score is given, should also penalize the batsman for getting out before his average score.
2. Give an example of numbers that have the same mean and standard deviation.
- (0, 0, 0, ...) will have the standard deviation 0 and mean 0.
The interviewer then asked for a non-trivial solution and asked whether (2, 0) will satisfy the given condition.
3. Describe hypothesis testing, what is significance level.

records.name: Saurav Rajput
records.resourcesWritten:
Use any standard JEE textbook for preparing quant. I used Cengage. For Cengage, go through the theory part completely, try to attempt the solved question given in between along with the exercises. If you are comfortable with these questions then you can ignore the exercises at the end of each chapter. This will be more than enough to secure 100% in quant. 1 month prior the exam, join any telegram group in which people posts questions daily. This will help you immensely.
For LR-DI-Verbal, use any standard CAT material. The level of PGDBA will be lower than it. In the last month try to practice at least 1 passage,  1 problem set of LR and DI each everyday.
Strategy - Focus on obtaining 35 questions of quant, LR, DI correct (easily attainable). If you can secure marks around 130/150, there will be less dependency on interview marks (very random) and you will have great chances.

VARC:

One can practice from previous year cat materials or something related to that and it will be enough. There would be some para jumbles and other verbal type questions too. Plus there are no TITA type questions.

questions.mathStats: The last panelist (I presume that he was from ISI) asked which topic of statistics was I most comfortable with. I replied in all honesty that I have zero background in statistics, not even at the UG level. Then I told him that I felt strong enough in Calculus and computational methods as far as mathematics is concerned. So, I was tested on the fundamentals of calculus. I was asked to definite continuity, distinguish it from differentiability and then give examples of functions that are continuous but not-differentiable and vice-versa. I was tested on differentiability of some functions posed by the panelist. In the end, he asked me to compute the integral of the greatest integer function from 1 to 10 without using any paper/pen/calculator. All questions were framed as a natural corollary to one another. There was a hint dropped when I was stuck in the middle of a question. There was however not much time given to think before responding.

questions.logical: My interview started with the first panelist straight away asking me why does a ship not sink even though it is so large. How does a yacht capsize? What are the types and directions of friction acting on 2 wheels of a bicycle? and so on. All the questions were from concepts involving class 12th level physics. I was found wanting in conceptual clarity in these topics.

records.name: Himanshu Mishra
records.resourcesWritten:
Be well versed with the basics of +2 level Mathematics. Practice enough to maximise your scores in this section. Refer any standard book for it and try to cover all the concepts.
VA section is a bit tricky so practice a lot of RCs.
records.resourcesInterview:
Cover the Statistics and Probability concepts really well. In case you are a fresher brush up your UG subjects too. Keep an open approach towards solving maths questions, your way of approaching the problem is what matters the most.
You should also cover PnC concepts and some basic Linear Algebra.
But all said you can't afford to miss out on current affairs and general basic economics concepts.
You will be asked questions about your job role if you are experienced.
Be confident and stay true to yourself, you will ace the interview.

questions.mathStats:
The first panalist  asked me to solve a problem I tried and I couldn't. I politely told the interviewer that I was not getting it. The panalist tried encouraging me to solve it I tried for a while but couldn't so I told him that I didn't want waste the time dwelling on that single problem. He said fine my work is done and passed on to the next panalist. I was expecting another problem from him but his response sent a couple of chills down my spine.
The next panelist asked me what did I know about statistics as I was from mechanical engineering background. I told him that we use statistical quality control in mechanical engineering and I told him that I have gone through a book called statistics for engineers by Anthony hater. He tested on that by giving different scenarios and asking what would be the probability distribution it would follow. I remember that the panelist had asked questions about distributions that were mentioned as optional/additional study in the book. I was so happy that I didn't skip those while studying.
He then asked about Memoryless property of distributions and then passed on to the third panalist.
